content:
morgan: customer ACME just reported their monthly credits went to 0 mid-flow during a large batch-embed job. they were running ~30 parallel workers with retries and started seeing 429s, then UI showed 0 and api continued to 429 until midnight refill. can we explain what likely happened and any quick mitigations?

sam: can you paste the customer repro steps and any request ids? did they see duplicate success responses or just 429s?

morgan: they sent this summary: 30 processes sending batches of 100 ids each to /v1/embeddings, with client-side retries on 5xx/timeouts (backoff 500ms->2s), many retries kicked in after a short network blip. logs show lots of successful 200s then a sudden flurry of retries, then sustained 429s. no request ids yet, asking customer for logs.

kai: hypothesis: in-flight duplicate requests from retries can cause multiple identical consumption events; our billing counts each completed request. if the primary succeeded but retry also completed (server-side eventual success), both are charged. also retries that time out client-side but still reach server will be charged.

ellie: customer says they used simple ephemeral ids per request and didn't include any idempotency keys. they're on org plan with monthly token bucket of 500M. observed drain from ~120M to 0 in ~7 minutes.

sam: that magnitude matches duplicate completions. we should check request logs for matching payloads around the window. can support pull a debug bundle (trace ids + request bodies) and I'll correlate. also check the X-Redwood-Quota header sequence if present.

infra-bot: alert: quota-drain spike detected for tenant acme-corp at 2025-09-12T21:13:08Z -> consumption rate ~17M tokens/min over 7 minutes. top endpoints: /v1/embeddings (78%), /v1/generate (12%).

morgan: customer also mentioned websocket reconnects from a streaming UI earlier during the same window — could streaming reconnects cause double-charge?

kai: streaming reconnects only bill for tokens actually accepted by the runtime. but if reconnect triggers new requests with overlapping context, you can end up re-sending prefixes and getting charged again. streaming does not automatically dedupe.

sam: short checklist for mitigation we recommend to customers: 1) add idempotency keys to batch requests (header X-Redwood-Idempotency or use request_id param) 2) limit parallelism / set client-side semaphore e.g., <=10 workers 3) add a short client dedupe cache for recent payloads 4) tune retry strategy to only retry on network errors, avoid retrying on 200/timeout ambiguous cases 5) enable request-level rate limit headers from our SDK.

ellie: can we provide an example snippet? acme wants a clear quick-fix.

sam: example (python):

```
import uuid
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer $KEY", "X-Redwood-Idempotency": str(uuid.uuid4())}
# ensure your retry library preserves this header per logical operation
```

sam: also recommend changing backoff: use jittered exponential and a short overall retry cap, e.g., max_retries=3, base=0.5s, max=2s.

morgan: billing question: customer expects a partial refund if duplicates consumed tokens. is that possible?

billing-bot: policy: we evaluate duplicate-consumption refund requests case-by-case. if there is clear evidence of server-side duplication or a platform bug (not client retries), we can issue credit. for client-triggered retries without idempotency, refunds are rare. please submit support ticket with debug bundle and we'll escalate.

kai: operational note for us: we should verify whether our ingestion side emitted a duplicate completion for the same request_id or trace_id. if server acked twice due to retryable backend failure that's on us. look for identical trace-id across two success events.

sam: I'll run a replay on a staging tenant to reproduce. quickly share a repro script for them (node) that spawns concurrent batches + aggressive retry to reproduce locally.

morgan: customer said they can run a test tonight. i'll send them the node script and ask for logs + the earliest trace ids after the spike.

ellie: also asked whether moving to dedicated capacity helps — will dedicated reduce risk?

kai: dedicated can reduce variability and capacity-driven requeues, but doesn't change client-side duplicate behavior. it reduces the chance of throttling-induced retries from overload. recommend dedicated only if they have sustained high throughput.

sam: followups for support: 1) ask customer to enable debug logs and send bundle 2) share idempotency header snippet and reduced parallelism guidance 3) offer a low-risk smoke test (10 workers, no retries) to confirm billing trend 4) escalate to billing if they request credit.

morgan: noted. i'll send the bundle request and the quick-fix instructions. thanks. :thumbsup: 

skip: closing note: also remind SDK teams to add idempotency header guidance to the batching docs (ticket opened ENG-1298).
